source_snapshot.procedure: Enter BMC Web, click the `Refresh` icon and verify that it refreshes.
source_snapshot.criteria: The icon function should be workable.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL replaces the in-application icon with browser F5, which exercises a different document, cache and session path.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION adds identity, safe-page, DOM/network, freshness and session controls, but permits either the UI control or browser reload.

old_problem: The historical record established objective refresh/freshness evidence but retained Pending for the exact page/widget, in-app selector, expected request, server-side freshness marker and session/cache contract.
disposition_reason: The source explicitly identifies the BMC application's Refresh icon, so F5/Ctrl-R cannot replace it. A Project-selected safe read-only page, control selector, expected read request, freshness/revalidation marker and session/cache behavior are normal runtime bindings. ED-08 requires real WebUI evidence, ED-20 preserves the icon-specific purpose, ED-35 records browser reload as non-equivalent, and ED-36 allows missing page/build values as prerequisites.
decision_basis: XLSX row 848, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record were directly reviewed.
The required evidence chain is in-app control event to intended read request/revalidation to completed rendered state; a spinner or unchanged screenshot alone cannot prove it.
A stable value may still be freshly retrieved, so PASS must rely on request/timestamp/ETag/sequence or other authoritative freshness metadata rather than arbitrary value change.
Pages with unsaved forms or pending configuration, firmware, credential, power or reset operations are excluded because refresh may repeat, cancel or obscure state.

test_case.test_name: Verify the BMC Web in-application Refresh control refetches and renders current data safely
test_case.purpose: Prove the BMC application's own Refresh icon is visible/enabled on an approved read-only page, triggers its version-defined read/revalidation path exactly once, completes the expected loading-to-ready DOM transition with current or freshly validated data, preserves the correct BMC/account/route/session behavior and causes no form, operation or duplicate mutation.
required_package: Immutable BMC identity, trusted Web URL/certificate, firmware/UI build and supported browser/version
Approved safe read-only page/widget, account/role, route and stable accessible/DOM selector for the in-app Refresh control
Authoritative data source and deterministic freshness evidence such as response timestamp, ETag, request ID, sequence/count, last-updated field or controlled external change
Expected read-only request/resource, loading/spinner lifecycle, DOM region, empty/error/stale state and completion timeout
Session/cookie/refresh-token behavior, route persistence, proxy/cache/service-worker contract and same-value revalidation expectation
Inventory proving no unsaved field, pending form/job, firmware/power/reset/credential/configuration action; protected session and evidence-redaction rules
test_case.test_command: Bind the browser to the exact BMC/UI build and approved read-only account/page, identify the application's Refresh control by stable semantic attributes and prove it is not browser reload. Confirm there is no unsaved or pending mutable operation. Record route, non-secret session identity, DOM baseline, authoritative data/freshness metadata and proxy/cache/service-worker context while arming network/console capture. Activate the in-app icon exactly once; correlate the event to the expected read/revalidation request, wait for the approved loading-to-ready condition, and record response ID/timestamp/ETag/sequence plus final DOM. Verify the same endpoint/account/route and documented session behavior, no mutating/duplicate request, no stale-cache result and no unexpected error/redirect. Do not use F5/Ctrl-R, clear cache/logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The visible enabled in-app Refresh control issues exactly the approved read/revalidation activity and reaches the ready state within the approved timeout. Returned metadata proves fresh retrieval or revalidation even when values are unchanged; the rendered data is usable and belongs to the same BMC/account/route. Session behavior matches policy and no form submission, configuration change, operation repeat, duplicate request, wrong-endpoint redirect or error occurs.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires one UI-control activation correlated to the expected read request/revalidation, authoritative freshness metadata, completed DOM state, correct endpoint/account/route/session and no mutation/duplicate/error, followed by engineer review. F5/Ctrl-R, icon animation, spinner completion, HTTP 200, changed text without identity or an unchanged screenshot cannot pass alone. Missing request, stale cache, stuck loading, logout/redirect contrary to policy, duplicate/mutating request, discarded unapproved state or wrong endpoint is FAIL. Missing page/selector/freshness/session contract is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Use the application's Refresh icon; browser F5, Ctrl-R, reload and away/back navigation test a different mechanism.
Select a read-only page with no unsaved form or pending power, firmware, reset, credential, configuration or long-running job; stop if refresh could repeat/cancel/obscure it.
Validate endpoint/certificate/build and protect credentials, cookies and tokens; post-refresh data must remain bound to the same BMC/account.
Correlate the click to a read-only request and server-side freshness/revalidation marker; do not accept animation or HTTP status alone.
Do not demand value change from a stable source; distinguish stable-but-fresh from stale by metadata.
Do not clear BMC/system/browser logs, cache or service-worker storage unless separately approved, because that changes the path and removes evidence.
No automatic retry; stop and preserve first-click network/DOM/session evidence on duplicate request, mutation, logout, redirect, wrong endpoint or stuck loading.
expected_evidence: BMC endpoint/certificate/device identity, firmware/UI build, browser/version, redacted account/role and approved page/widget route
Pre-click screenshot/DOM with in-app Refresh selector and visible/enabled state plus proof no unsaved/pending operation exists
Baseline rendered data, authoritative freshness metadata and proxy/cache/service-worker context
Single click event mapped to expected read request/response with request ID, timestamp/ETag/sequence and loading-to-ready transition
Final DOM/screenshot with same BMC/account/route/session and stable-fresh versus stale determination
Network/console evidence of no duplicate/mutating request or error, first-attempt artifact and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If refresh loses access, discards state, duplicates/mutates a request or reaches the wrong endpoint, stop without another click, preserve first-attempt route/session/network/DOM evidence and close the isolated session. Use only the documented re-login/OOB path to restore access; do not resubmit an operation or reconstruct unapproved data automatically.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require the BMC application's Refresh icon; page and freshness bindings are underspecified but not contradictory.

blocked.reason: The in-app operation and expected refresh behavior are identifiable; safe page, selector, request, freshness and session markers are supplyable inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: BMC/UI build, safe read-only page/widget, in-app selector, expected request, freshness/readiness markers, cache/service-worker/session contract and no-pending-state inventory.

project_authority: The version-matched Project/vendor BMC UI control and page-data contract define the in-app refresh request, readiness, freshness and session behavior; generic browser reload is not authoritative for this case.
